# Proposal Phase 2

This section of the proposal will add more detail as well as Storyboard Sketches (You should revise the previous sections if needed and add storyboard sketches)

## User Experience: Input/Output and Wireflow

You must create a wireflow diagram that shows **all** of your screens for your design. This is a combination of wireframe diagrams. This will include any user input/output that is needed to control your application including mouse and keyboard interaction.

**Wireframe screens:** These are the rough sketches of the key screens in your app. They’re usually shown as boxes with basic shapes like rectangles for buttons, lines for text, and dropdowns or checkboxes to represent interactions. If a screen changes its UI state you may duplicate it. Note the different states for those screens.  *Note: You must show all three versions of your design here. You can show this by using different colors for each part of your design (prototype, core and stretch) so you can see how it will function at each phase*

**Arrows:** These connect the screens and show how users move from one to the next. Straight lines indicate simple navigation, while branching arrows can show decision branches or alternative paths. *Note: You must show arrows from an exact point of a click to the destination screen. If your diagram becomes unwieldy, you may reduce the number of arrows by labelling in and out points of arrows with a number instead such as (1, 2,3 etc)*

**Notes and annotations:** Easily provide helpful context to explain things like button behavior, system feedback (like error messages), or any behind-the-scenes logic you want to capture. These are usually shown as callouts, sticky notes, or small text labels next to the wireframes.

- See examples of wireflows and a longer description [here](https://balsamiq.com/blog/wireflows/)

## Test Plan

Define how you are going to test that your code is working correctly, how you will test edge conditions or errors happening and so forth. Make sure to build time in your schedule to get this done. This should be very detailed on steps to follow to complete a test pass (you will be thankful you have this so you can run through these tests before each of the sprint demo's on Friday's). You should label your tests with the milestone needed to run that test (since you won't have all the functionality to run all the tests until the work is completed)

An example for a testing strategy may be something like the following. **Note**: You will need to provide detailed steps for manual testing that describe which screens you will view, what you would click on and what the expected behavior is. For the Prototype testing, provide at least 5 questions for your peers to provide feedback to you for your specific application.

| Test Category | Details |
| :---- | :---- |
| Prototype Testing | At prototype we will provide students X,Y,Z our application with a sheet to fill in answers to the following questions: \- What can be improved? \- What did each of the icons on the main screen mean to you? \- \_etc\_ |
| Manual Testing | Before each demo we will do the following manual tests: \- Go to main screen and click X, and make sure Y comes up \- \_etc\_ many more |
| Automated testing | We will implement automated tests for the following classes/methods:  \- MainScreen.java (all of it) \- CustomScreen.java:specialCalc \- \_etc\_ |
| *Other testing* | Any other type of testing you might be thinking of |

## Our version: 

| Test Category | Details |
| :---- | :---- |
| Prototype Testing | At prototype we will provide students X,Y,Z our application with a sheet to fill in answers to the following questions: \- What can be improved? \- What did each of the icons on the main screen mean to you? \- \_etc\_ Prototype features: Title screen with a button that says “start game” The “start game” button leads to Menu with multiple buttons including “settings”, “important info”, “help” and “start” When you click start, you will be taken to the starting position with four doors When you click on one of the four doors, it will take you inside Click the “back button” when you want to exit the room Click the “go home” button when you are done Click on the speech bubble to see stats When you are at the starting position and can see the four classrooms, what can we make more clear on how you are able to enter the classrooms (clicking on door). Did you know how to enter the classrooms or did you have to go to the help tab before?  When the game began with the “Alarm Screen”, how can we make the animation more engaging and more likely for the player to continue the game?  What was interactive about the layout of the four classrooms? Did they become repetitive? What can we improve about the sprite character, design wise? In the Library Classroom, was the sprite interacting smoothly with its surrounding objects (bookshelves, tables, students, etc) When moving from the starting position to the classrooms and vice versa, was the movement smooth? What could be improved about the animation, (fade out and fade in the new screen? Blackout the screen and then show the new screen?) After you completed the game, was the main goal, raising awareness of the struggles of those with invisible disabilities, clear? How can we integrate this theme through the entire game, not just the important info screen at the end.  What did you like and dislike about the perspective of the character (would top down be better, can you see your surroundings well)? |
| Manual Testing | Before each demo we will do the following manual tests: Prototype: \- Start on the title screen and click the “start” button and make sure it goes to the menu screen \- Go to Menu after the starting page, click “wake up” and make sure the starting position shows up \- Go to Menu after the starting page, click help and a guide on how to play the game should show up \- Go to starting position and click a door, and make sure the screen changes to that room \- Go to one of the four rooms in which there are tasks to complete and click the back button, this should take us to the starting position (keep going til all tasks done) \- Go to starting position after all tasks are completed and the “go home” button should appear  \- Once you click the “go home” button, it should take you to the stats screen (home) \- Once home, a box above the character’s mom’s head will appear, and when clicked, stats will show \- After a couple seconds, an important info button will show up. When clicked, it should change the screen to the important info text.  Core: \- In the starting position, there is a task list dropdown. Click it, and all the tasks from all the rooms should show up \- Once at home, the character’s mom should be in the kitchen and ask “How was your day?”. Once you click on the speech bubble, the statistics for the game should appear. (Statistics would include: social battery, popularity score, tasks done-like a yes or no thing) Stretch: \- We were planning on adding more rooms for stretch, so when clicked on the fifth and sixth door, the same thing (enter room, complete tasks) will happen \- Go to the starting position and click on the audio button. Music should start playing. \- Once home, mom will also ask you to tell you about the day. When clicked, video clips of the game will show up (kind of like a video summary of the game you played.) \- In the rooms, when moving closer to your task, instead of just conversations with the person, there will be side conversations, bringing down the social battery a little bit, and there will be more ambiguity in the responses because it’ll be a longer conversation.  |
| Automated testing | We will create automated tests that check the following: \- sprites (player, NPCs, inanimate objects) do not overlap when in the same ‘layer’ of the scene → we will move around the sprites using WASD and see if they overlap \- picking a choice onscreen (a button) matches the correct choice (the text)/path associated with the choice → we will click on the door and see if it goes to the room that we designed \- a given choice causes a given thing to happen (similar to, but different from the previous test) → we will click on a response that the user can pick and see if it garners the “correct reaction from the npc” \- in-game tasks are logged as completed when the player completes them → when a player completes a task, the checkbox in the dropdown should automatically check off |
| *Other testing* | Any other type of testing you might be thinking of |
